a.fixed: When the children reached the cave, they saw that the door was broken.
a.why: When starts the part that cannot stand alone, so a comma goes after cave. Reached and saw are both past tense.

b.raw: when lucy saw the robin she asked it where mr tumnus was
b.fixed: When Lucy saw the robin, she asked it where Mr. Tumnus was.
b.why: When starts the part that cannot stand alone, so a comma goes after robin. Lucy and Mr. Tumnus are names. Saw and asked are both past tense.

cards.title: World Notes: Robins in Winter
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read the chapter with your lens in mind.
text: The robin in Narnia is a European robin: a small brown bird with an orange-red breast.
In Britain, robins stay all winter and sing even in the cold, so people often see them in the snow.
That is one reason robins are on so many British Christmas cards.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. All four children are in Narnia now. Watch what they choose when they find Mr. Tumnus's cave.
transcripts.guide1: Word work: build form words, keep every verb in the past, and split long words into beats.
transcripts.guide2: Read Chapter 6. Then answer three questions.
transcripts.guide3: Today you put your whole paragraph together.

notes.wordParts: The root form means shape. uniform = one shape for everyone. transform = to change shape.
notes.grammar: Keep your verbs in the same time. If a story starts in the past (walked, ate), every verb stays in the past.
notes.spelling: Every beat in a word has one vowel sound. Count the sounds, not the letters: de-tail has two beats.
notes.wgrd: Some choices are brave. Lucy chooses to help Mr. Tumnus because he got into trouble for helping her.

mods.script: [warmly] Here's today's reading tip. Some choices are brave. When the children find Mr. Tumnus's cave, they have to choose: go on, or go home? Watch who wants what. Then tap one of the two lenses below to use while you read. You don't need to write anything.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. The correct one first. When the children climbed into the wardrobe, they pushed past the coats and stepped into the snow. Climbed, pushed and stepped all stay in the past. Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Say the parts out loud. Type the whole word in each box. Tap Check My Answers.
mods.script: Snap the parts together. Form. At. Format! The format of a page is its shape: where the title goes, and where the words go. Say each pair of parts out loud. Type the whole word in the box. Then tap Check My Answers.

mods.todo: Read each sentence. Pick the word that fits.
mods.script: Try each word in the blank, and keep the one that makes sense. Here's my sentence. Edmund gave Lucy a blank look, as if he were much older. Beastly? Hmm, no. Superior? Yes! Now pick the word that fits each sentence.

mods.todo: Read the before and after. Rewrite the sentences in the past tense.
mods.script: Let's move a sentence into the past. The children run upstairs and hide in the wardrobe. Run becomes ran. Hide becomes hid. The children ran upstairs and hid in the wardrobe. Read the before and after. Then rewrite the two sentences so every verb is in the past.

mods.todo: Read the rule. Say each word in chunks. Tap the card to see the beats.
mods.script: Let's split a long word into chunks. Professor. Pro, fes, sor. Three chunks! Say each chunk, then push them back together: Professor. Read the rule. Then say each word in chunks, and tap the card to check.

mods.todo: Answer each question in full sentences. Use details from the book.
mods.script: Three questions, in full sentences. One, three details about Mr. Tumnus's cave. Two, Lucy's reason for helping him, and whether it convinces you. Three, why Lewis might choose a robin as a guide.

virtue.name: honesty
virtue.title: Truth Watch: Is someone being honest?

items.t: Edmund pretends he has never been in the wood before.
items.why: He had been there. Pretending is not honest.

items.t: Peter says out loud that Edmund made out Lucy was telling lies.
items.why: He tells the truth about what Edmund did.

items.t: Lucy says the Faun is in trouble because he helped her, so they must try to rescue him.
items.why: She owns up to her part, even though it means danger.
